Exploring VICFREIGHT

Source: vignettes/exploring-vicfreight.Rmd
exploring-vicfreight.Rmd

Introduction

VICFREIGHT is an R package for exploring Victorian road traffic activity, with an emphasis on heavy-vehicle movements, vehicle composition, traffic patterns across monitoring locations and reporting completeness.

It is intended for users interested in investigating how traffic activity varies across monitoring locations and time. The package combines prepared traffic datasets, analytical functions and an interactive Shiny dashboard.

This vignette introduces the included datasets, explains how to install and launch the dashboard, and describes how to interpret its main outputs.

Installation

The package can be installed directly from its GitHub repository using devtools.

install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-vikywayne"
)

Once installed, load the package:

library(vicfreight)

Included datasets

VICFREIGHT includes three prepared datasets:

  • traffic_counts: Traffic observations recorded at monitoring locations, including dates, fifteen-minute intervals, vehicle classifications, headings, speed categories and traffic volumes.
  • telemetry_sites: Monitoring site descriptions and geographic coordinates.
  • site_day_coverage: Reporting coverage for each monitoring site and date, including the number of intervals reported and whether the day is complete.

The datasets can be accessed after installing the package.

data("traffic_counts", package = "vicfreight")
data("telemetry_sites", package = "vicfreight")
data("site_day_coverage", package = "vicfreight")

head(traffic_counts)
head(telemetry_sites)
head(site_day_coverage)

The package includes a prepared snapshot of traffic monitoring data covering May to October 2026. The included datasets are fixed to this collection period and are not automatically refreshed when new observations become available from the original data source. The data-raw scripts document the preparation process used to generate the packaged datasets.

The traffic observations are recorded in fifteen-minute intervals. A complete reporting day is expected to contain 96 intervals for a monitoring site.

Incomplete reporting days and traffic observations without matching site metadata are retained in the prepared datasets. This allows users to examine reporting coverage and recognise limitations in the available site information.

Launching the dashboard

The package includes an interactive Shiny dashboard. It can be launched using the exported run_vicfreight() function.

vicfreight::run_vicfreight()

The dashboard uses the datasets included in the installed package. Users do not need to download or provide the original CSV files to run the application.

Using the dashboard

The dashboard contains four main sections.

Overview

The Overview section introduces the monitoring locations and provides a geographical view of traffic activity. It also presents traffic summary information and vehicle composition.

Users can explore the monitoring locations and use the playback controls to examine how the displayed traffic activity changes over the selected time sequence.

The map represents monitoring locations and their recorded activity. It should not be interpreted as showing individual vehicle movements or vehicle routes.

Site comparison

The Site comparison section allows users to select monitoring locations, a date range and a vehicle classification.

The displayed chart and summary table update according to these selections. This helps users compare recorded traffic volumes across selected sites and examine differences in activity over the chosen period.

When interpreting comparisons, users should consider the reporting coverage of the selected sites. A lower recorded volume may reflect incomplete reporting as well as lower observed traffic activity.

Traffic trends

The Traffic trends section allows users to examine traffic activity over daily or monthly periods. Users can select monitoring locations, date ranges and vehicle classifications.

The time-series chart helps identify changes and patterns in recorded traffic volumes over time. The accompanying summary table provides the corresponding aggregated values.

Daily trends can reveal shorter-term changes, while monthly summaries provide a broader view of activity. Gaps in reporting should be considered when interpreting apparent changes in the series.

Reporting coverage

The Reporting coverage section examines the completeness of traffic reporting across monitoring locations and dates.

It includes summaries of complete and incomplete site-days, reporting coverage by month, average reported intervals by site and a table of incomplete reporting days.

A complete site-day contains all 96 expected fifteen-minute intervals. An incomplete site-day contains fewer than 96 reported intervals.

This section is important when interpreting the other dashboard outputs. Traffic summaries are based on recorded observations, so incomplete reporting may affect comparisons and apparent trends.

Interpreting the outputs

The dashboard supports exploration of three related aspects of Victorian traffic monitoring:

  1. Traffic activity: Recorded traffic volumes and how they vary across monitoring locations and time.
  2. Vehicle composition: The distribution of recorded vehicle classifications and the relative contribution of different vehicle groups.
  3. Reporting coverage: The completeness of the observations used to examine traffic activity.

These aspects should be considered together. For example, differences in traffic volumes between two monitoring locations should not automatically be interpreted as differences in actual traffic activity without considering whether both locations have comparable reporting coverage.

Similarly, an apparent change in a daily traffic trend should be considered alongside any missing reporting intervals during the relevant period.

Analytical functions

In addition to the dashboard, VICFREIGHT provides exported functions for working with the included traffic data:

  • summarise_traffic() summarises traffic observations using selected grouping variables and filters.
  • compare_sites() compares traffic activity across selected monitoring locations.
  • summarise_vehicle_mix() summarises vehicle composition and percentage shares.
  • summarise_traffic_trends() summarises traffic activity over daily or monthly periods.

Detailed usage information for each function is available in the package reference documentation.

Limitations

The outputs describe recorded traffic observations rather than a complete census of all road movements. Reporting gaps, incomplete site-days and unmatched site metadata should be considered when interpreting results.

The monitoring locations also represent specific points in the road network. Their observations should not automatically be treated as representative of all roads or traffic across Victoria.

The dashboard is intended to support exploratory investigation and comparison, rather than establish causal explanations for observed traffic patterns.

Conclusion

VICFREIGHT brings together prepared Victorian traffic data, analytical functions and an interactive dashboard to support the exploration of freight-related road activity.

By examining traffic volumes, vehicle composition and reporting coverage together, users can investigate patterns across monitoring locations while recognising the limitations of the available observations.
